position: fixed removes .badge from flow. top: 10px and left: 12px locate it from its containing block. In the worked fixture no ancestor establishes a fixed containing block, so that is the preview iframe viewport, not the outer application window.

Use fixed UI sparingly: it can cover content, especially when zoomed. A transformed ancestor is one common exception to viewport anchoring; containment and related properties can also change this behavior.

after: The viewport is the visible page area. `position: fixed` usually places an element relative to that area. It takes the element out of normal page flow, so other content leaves no space for it.
A containing block is the area used to place and size an element. Here, the badge's reference is the preview's viewport, not the whole app window.
A transform on a parent can make that parent the fixed badge's reference instead. Even `transform: translateX(0px)` can do this. Zero means no visible shift, but the transform still exists.
A fixed element can cover other content. Check small screens and zoomed text to make sure the page stays usable.

before.question: Can transform: translateX(0px) on an ancestor change fixed positioning even though it moves nothing?
choices: No, zero always means no other effect
Yes, it can establish the containing block
Only if the badge uses absolute positioning
before.explanation: A non-none transform affects containing-block formation even at zero displacement.

after.question: Can a parent's translateX(0px) change what a fixed badge is positioned against?
choices: No, zero can never have another effect
Yes, the parent can become the reference area
Only when the badge is absolute
after.explanation: The transform can create a new reference area even when it moves the parent by zero pixels.
